Real campus spice throughput is much larger than the retail figure.

32% of category value (₹5.09 L) comes from just 12 bills through the 'Basement' warehouse — the mess/langar indent. Every weight-priced '_L' SKU sells ONLY there, at exactly 5 bills each. So ARY has an institutional bulk desk but NO retail buy-by-gram spice counter, which is the single highest-margin item on the ideal list.

Zero Everest spices. India's largest spice brand (~3.5 bn packs/yr) has 3 SKUs at ARY — a green chilli sauce, a snack topping and a vinegar — and all three are dormant. The rack runs on MDH + Catch + Ruchi + Sunil + unbranded local, plus Jivo own-label.

Jivo (the parent company) own-label spices are on the shelf: Jivo Black Pepper 100 Gm (45 bills), Jivo Cumin Seeds 100 Gm (40), Jivo Cinnamon Sticks 100 Gm (24), Jivo Green Cardamom 100 Gm (30) — the cardamom filed under 'Rice & Other Grains > Pulses & Lenitils'.

A pahari/Punjabi winter-and-post-natal cluster the ideal list never named, and it moves: Gond Kachira 50Gm (278 bills, ₹11,135), Mulethi 50 Gm (195 bills), Magaj / melon seeds (92 bills, ₹9,580), Kamarkash 100Gm/50Gm, Sabu Dana 100 Gm, Harad 50 Gm, Sunil Sandal Powder. Gond + magaj are the panjiri/laddoo inputs; sabudana is the fasting staple that pairs with sendha namak.
Ajinomoto (MSG) is stocked in 500 g at retail (Ajinomoto 500 Gm, Golden Crown Ajinomoto 500 Gm) — a canteen input the ideal list never considered; both currently dormant at POS.
Ruchi Black Salt 100Gm does 664 bills — the 6th most frequently bought SKU in the category, ahead of every branded haldi or mirch. Kala namak massively over-indexes here.

Maggi Masala Magic ₹5 sachet is the #1 spice SKU by frequency (3,916 bills, ₹44,880). Low-unit-price formats dominate throughout: Catch Long Whole ₹10 (595 bills), Catch Elichi ₹10 (471), S&J GG paste 30 Gm (374), Savour Green Cardamom 3 Gm (302) — while nearly every 500 g and 1 kg retail pack is dormant.

60% of the shelf list is dead: only 207 of 518 active SKUs sold in 12 months, driven by duplicate-code sprawl — 14 Kasoori Methi codes (4 sell), 'Catch Ajwain 100 Gm' / '100Gm' / '100Gms' as three codes (one sells), 'Ruchi Red Chilli Powder 100 Gm' as three codes, 'Appu Termaric Powder 100 Gm' twice, 'Shrinath Ji Sabat Dhania 100 Gm' twice.

Group coding is unreliable — search by name, never by group: 'Chips', 'Chips Gol Gappa' and 'Soya Katori' are filed under Salt & Sugar > Salt; Dabur Meswak (a toothpaste) and Del Monte Beans under Spices > Spices Paste; 9 Saffola Masala Oats SKUs under Spices > Masala; the four Keya 7 g Italian/peri-peri sachets under Salt & Sugar > Salt; MTR upma/dhokla/vada ready-mixes and 7 custard powders under Spices.

Monthly data confirms the pickle-season thesis and the gap: category sales sat at ₹90k-140k/month through 2025, then spiked to ₹2.68 L (May-26) and ₹2.20 L (Jun-26) — and ARY has no achar masala, no pickling kit, no coarse yellow sarson and no crystal dhela salt to sell into that window. It sells ~55 finished pickle SKUs instead.

Warehouse-level oddity worth flagging to the operator: Ary Pos shows ₹9,99,722 of 'excess' and ₹1,73,550 of 'shortage' in the physical-count columns, and Ary Clothing carries a negative book stock of -323,760 units. Also, the sales feed stops at 2026-08-21 (SaleHeader latest) while accounting runs to 2026-08-27 — the 12m window used here is 2025-08-21 to 2026-08-22.
